videos.title: The Easy Way to Fix Boring UIs
videos.why: Sajid's approach to depth with shades and layered shadows, including a three-shadow example on CodePen you can copy; compare his levels with the ones you build in lab-elevation.

videos.title: WWDC25: Meet Liquid Glass | Apple
videos.why: Apple's newest material for controls that float above content; the principles section at 10:31 covers where this layer belongs and where it should stay out of the way.

podcasts.episode: 71: The materials interfaces are made of
podcasts.why: Two interface designers on why screens imitate physical materials such as paper or metal, which ones are most common and how that has shifted over time; useful context for shadows, surfaces and glass.

reads.title: Designing Beautiful Shadows in CSS
reads.why: Interactive demos of a consistent light source, layered shadows and shadows tinted to the background; the reference for turning elevation levels into real box-shadow values.

reads.title: Visual design rules you can safely follow every time
reads.why: Read 'Nest corners properly', 'Closer elements should be lighter', 'Make drop shadow blur values double their distance values' and 'Don't mix depth techniques' first; the rest of the list is worth keeping too.

reads.title: Elevation
reads.why: Elevation as distance on the z-axis, shown with tonal surface colour or shadow; note Google's own advice to use only a few levels and to save shadows for when they are needed.
